monitor.heading: Monitor
log.empty: Sent and received data will appear here after you run.
watch.errorWs: WS error — switching to HTTP polling
watch.mapUnavailable: Cannot generate monitor addresses from the connection settings.
watch.noteUnavailable: Monitoring is available when connected via PLCLINK / Field Network.
watch.notePlclink: Generated automatically from the command / response / PLO / PLI settings. You can change the number of words shown for the command and response views. Update period: {interval} ms. Bit pulse width is taken from the write time, so ON/OFF shorter than the watch period is also shown with the width received.
watch.noteFieldNetwork: "Result data" shows "Output value" (raw DWORD) and "Data" (interpreted value), as in VTV. Update period: {interval} ms (WebSocket). Bit changes are recorded at packet arrival time. Width resolution is the RPI, minimum 2 ms. An RPI of 1 ms is invalid.
watch.noteStatic: Generated automatically from the command / response / PLO assignments in the connection settings.
watch.reloadTitle: Regenerate the list from the connection settings
watch.intervalTitle: Monitor update interval (ms). Minimum 1 ms. With WebSocket delivery the server pushes at this period.
watch.actualTitle: Measured polling start interval (smoothed). The value in parentheses is the most recent HTTP fetch time.
watch.commandWordsTitle: Number of words shown from the start of the command area. The upper limit is the command size in the connection settings. If you set it equal to the size, the view extends to the end even when the size is increased.
watch.responseWordsTitle: Number of words shown from the start of the response area. The upper limit is the response size in the connection settings. For long responses such as 30000, enlarge the size and this value together.
watch.resultDataTitle: Corresponds to the "Output value / Data" columns of the VTV result data output monitor
timing.zoomInTitle: Zoom in on the time axis (mouse wheel up also works)
timing.zoomInAria: Zoom in on the time axis
timing.zoomOutTitle: Zoom out on the time axis (mouse wheel down also works)
timing.zoomOutAria: Zoom out on the time axis
timing.zoomResetTitle: Reset the view width and follow the latest data
timing.axisTitle: Poll count: the horizontal axis is linear in real time, and ticks sit at the real time of each poll. Real time: evenly spaced time ticks.
timing.actualTitle: Measured polling start interval (smoothed). The value in parentheses is the most recent read time.
timing.measureInfoDefault: The horizontal axis is linear in real time. Ticks are at each poll's real time (spacing changes if the period jitters). Click to place A/B.
timing.hintPollSelect: The horizontal axis is linear in real time. Ticks are at each poll's real time position (spacing changes if the period jitters). Click outside the chart to clear the selection.
timing.hintTimeSelect: Both the horizontal axis and ticks are in real time (evenly spaced). To check poll-to-poll variation, the "Poll count" axis is recommended. Click outside the chart to clear the selection.
timing.hintPollMeasure: The horizontal axis is linear in real time. Ticks are at each poll's real time (spacing changes if the period jitters). Click to place A/B. Click outside the chart to clear.
timing.hintTimeMeasure: Both the horizontal axis and ticks are in real time. Click to place cursors A/B (Δt and signal length). Click outside the chart to clear.
timing.cursorClickB: Click B to measure the interval
timing.note: Click to measure, use the wheel to zoom the time axis, and use the bar below to move the view. Bit widths follow the time of change; other values follow the watch period.
timing.selectSignalPrompt: Select the bit signals to compare from the list on the left
timing.noWaveform: There is no waveform to export.
settings.title: Connection & protocol settings
settings.hintTcp: Connects as a client to the device's Network I/O (TCP).
settings.hintPlclink: The app listens on all NICs as a soft PLC (MC 3E). Press "Start soft PLC listening" first, then set the VTV destination to this PC's LAN IP:listen port.
settings.hintFieldNetwork: The app connects to VTV (Adapter) as an EtherNet/IP Scanner. The destination is the VTV unit's IP (LAN1/LAN2, port 44818). In VTV, turn ON "Enable field network (normal)", and import the created EDS into both so that the sizes match.
settings.virtualIoRangeDefault: Virtual input M0–M31 / virtual output M1024–M1055. Use the same start addresses as the VTV virtual I/O.
settings.virtualIoRange: Virtual input M{pliStart}–M{pliEnd} / virtual output M{ploStart}–M{ploEnd}. Use the same start addresses as the VTV virtual I/O.
settings.busyAddressHintDefault: BUSY actual address: M1024 (PLO start + port number - 1). Match the VTV "Status signal" assignment.
settings.busyAddressHint: BUSY actual address: M{busy} (PLO start M{plo} + Port {port} - 1 / port count {portCount}). {count} monitored signals. Match the VTV "Status signal" assignment.
settings.statusSignalsNotePlclink: Used for the monitor display and for waiting on BUSY in commands. Signals are assigned to virtual output (PLO) ports. Exactly one signal with role=BUSY is required.
settings.statusSignalsNoteFn: Used for the monitor display and for waiting on BUSY in commands. Signals are assigned to a status-area bit or an ESO port. Exactly one signal with role=busy is required.
settings.signalDeleteBusyRequired: At least one signal is required for BUSY
settings.errBusyCount: Exactly one status signal with role=BUSY is required (currently {count}).
settings.errNoEso: Signal "{label}": cannot assign to ESO because the ESO port count is 0
settings.errEsoExceeds: Signal "{label}": ESO-{port} exceeds the configured port count {count}
settings.errPloExceeds: Signal "{label}": PLO-{port} exceeds the virtual output port count {count}
settings.portNamesPlclinkNote: Give ports easy-to-read names for D/M monitoring and local I/O. Blank entries show only the port number.
settings.portNamesFnNote: Give ports easy-to-read names for D/M monitoring. Blank entries show only ESI-N / ESO-N.
settings.resultWatchWordsTitle: Number of leading words shown in D/M monitoring
settings.resultDecimalsTitle: Match the decimal places in the VTV detailed settings
settings.resultNote1: The result data area is always shown in D/M monitoring (from the start up to the watch display word count). Real numbers are written as fixed-point (integer × 10^decimals), so switch the "Result data" notation in the monitor to match the VTV monitor.
settings.resultNote2: Use the same values as VTV "Environment settings → PLCLINK". The connection test waits for a connection from VTV.
settings.fnEdsStatusDefault: Loads an EDS created in VTV and applies the size / RPI / path.
settings.fnRpiTitle: I/O update period (μs). The device minimum is 2000 (2 ms). 1000 (1 ms) is invalid.
settings.fnLayoutHintDefault: The assigned sizes must match the EDS input/output sizes.
settings.fnLayoutCalc: Layout calculation: input {calcIn} bytes / output {calcOut} bytes (EDS: input {inSize} / output {outSize})
settings.fnLayoutMismatch: — mismatch. Adjust ESI/ESO, word counts, or the EDS.
settings.fnNote: The app connects to VTV (Adapter) as an EtherNet/IP Scanner. The port is normally 44818. It cannot be used together with PLCLINK.
settings.fnResultNote: The word count is included in the Assembly input size. Match it with the layout calculation on the Destination page.
settings.fnEdsImported: Import complete: {name} (IN {in} / OUT {out} / ESI {esi} / ESO {eso} / CMD {cmd} / RPI {rpi}μs)

help.title: Guide
help.tcpBody: This PC connects to the device's Network I/O. Enter the device IP and port, run the connection test, then run.
help.plclinkBody: This app listens as a soft PLC. Press "Start soft PLC listening" first, then set the VTV destination to this PC's LAN IP and the listen port.
help.fnBody: This app is the Scanner and VTV is the Adapter. The port is normally 44818. Do not use it at the same time as PLCLINK.
help.firewallBody: Allow the PLCLINK listen port and Field Network port 44818. For TCP, the device must accept connections from this PC.
help.busyLine1: BUSY is the signal that the device is processing. A command waits for BUSY to drop before moving on to the next.
help.busyLine2: AK means the response is complete. NK means no response. ER means an error.
help.historyNote: Open a row to read the communication of that run.
tour.heading: On-screen guides
tour.intro: Highlighted walkthroughs. The basics guide starts automatically on first launch. Exit anytime with Close (×) or Esc.
tour.basics.title: Basics
tour.basics.desc: Layout, adding cards, and running a sequence
tour.basics.s1Body: Connection status, Run/Stop, connection settings, and Help live here.
tour.basics.s2Body: Choose the transport (TCP / PLCLINK / Field Network) and destination here.
tour.basics.s2bBody: At the top right, you can turn PLI (PLCLINK) or ESI (Field Network) ports ON/OFF directly — even while a sequence is running. This control is hidden for TCP.
tour.basics.s3Body: Click a card on the left to append it to the sequence on the right.
tour.basics.s3bBody: Example: a Delay card moving into the sequence. In real use, click a card to add it.
tour.basics.s4Body: Cards run from top to bottom. Drag the handle to reorder.
tour.basics.s5Body: After the connection is verified, send the sequence to the device (Ctrl+Enter).
tour.basics.s6Body: Logs, watch values, and timing charts. See the Monitor guide for details.
tour.tcp.title: TCP connection
tour.tcp.desc: Connect to Network I/O and run
tour.tcp.s1Body: With TCP (Network I/O), this PC connects out to the device.
tour.tcp.s3Body: Enter the device Network I/O IP address.
tour.tcp.s4Body: The device listen port (often 55555; match the device setting).
tour.tcp.s5Body: Run a connection test before executing a sequence.
tour.tcp.s6Body: Save once the values look correct.
tour.tcp.s7Body: After arranging cards, press Run to send them to the device.
tour.plclink.title: PLCLINK connection
tour.plclink.desc: Soft PLC listening and VTV-side setup
tour.plclink.s1Body: With PLCLINK, this app listens as a soft PLC.
tour.plclink.s3Body: Use this PC's LAN IP (or 0.0.0.0). Put the same IP in the VTV destination.
tour.plclink.s4Body: Match the VTV PLCLINK destination port.
tour.plclink.s5Body: Start listening first, then connect from VTV. Allow the port in the firewall.
tour.plclink.s6Body: Save address maps and BUSY settings so they match VTV.
tour.plclink.s7Body: Check listen / connection status from the badge.
tour.fn.title: Field Network connection
tour.fn.s1Body: This app is the Scanner and VTV is the Adapter. Do not use PLCLINK at the same time.
tour.fn.s3Body: Enter the VTV (Adapter) IP. The port is normally 44818.
tour.fn.s4Body: Import an EDS from VTV to apply sizes, RPI, and the connection path.
tour.fn.s5Body: Start the connection. Ensure port 44818 is allowed in the firewall.
tour.fn.s7Body: Check connection status from the badge.
tour.monitor.title: Monitor
tour.monitor.desc: Logs, port selection, and expanded view
tour.monitor.s1Body: The right-hand panel for results and signal watch.
tour.monitor.s2Body: Inspect TX/RX over time. Filtering and export are here too.
tour.monitor.s3Body: Lists mapped command / response / I/O (port) values (PLCLINK / Field Network).
tour.monitor.s3bBody: Built automatically from connection mappings. Check the values of the ports and signals you care about here.
tour.monitor.s3cBody: Search by signal name, or show only changed signals, to find the ports you need.
tour.monitor.s4Body: Starts periodic reads. You can also change the update interval here.
tour.monitor.s5Body: Record and measure bit waveforms. Recording starts after watch begins.
tour.monitor.s5bBody: In the left list, check the ports / bits you want on the timing chart. Selecting only what you need keeps it readable.
tour.monitor.s6Body: Use Expand on the panel when you want a monitor-only layout for watch or timing.
tour.monitor.s7Body: This is the expanded view. The watch list gets more room, so port values are easier to follow.
tour.monitor.s8Body: Even while expanded, pick ports / bits for the waveform from the left list.
tour.monitor.s9Body: Use the header button (or Esc) to return to the normal layout with cards and monitor side by side.
